reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes purchasing Thor tokens to create paid nodes that supposedly provide recurring daily rewards and passive income, while emphasizing sustainability and life-changing earning potential. It gives step-by-step instructions to buy the tokens, connect a wallet, and create a node, despite stating that the node purchase cannot be refunded and requires continuing monthly maintenance fees. The creator then directly encourages viewers to enter related crypto opportunities through his mentorship link.

you just have to connect your wallet and you should see the amount of solid that you have right up here. So you scroll down and you choose which node you would like to create. You simply name your node here. And after naming your node, then you simply hit right here where it says create node.

opening.argument: Judge, this is investment commentary that gives viewers material reasons to be cautious. The speaker says the tokens spent to create a node cannot be recovered directly and identifies monthly maintenance fees; he also reports that rewards were cut in half. Those are consequential drawbacks, not a promise of fixed earnings. His assessment of the change is explicitly an opinion, and the description tells viewers to do their own research. The optimistic language should be read alongside those disclosures, not in isolation.

This is not explicit advice to buy these cryptos, do your own research.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker describes daily rewards and walks through buying tokens. But its own nonrefundability quote shows that he also explains a serious cost of participation. The purchase walkthrough establishes how a viewer could create a node, not that the speaker guarantees a return or conceals the downside. Likewise, the broad claim about life-changing crypto wealth does not specify that this node will deliver it.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings and a disclaimer do not erase the pitch. The speaker links an upfront token purchase to daily node rewards, then gives viewers the steps to buy the token and create a node. Disclosing that the payment cannot be recovered makes the financial exposure clearer; it does not turn the promoted paid-node return into mere market commentary.

opening.argument: Judge, the central presentation is a walkthrough of a project's mechanics. The speaker says he is using its own PDF, explains the different node entry levels, and describes what happens when rewards are claimed or compounded. He also identifies where viewers can find the source document themselves. The later purchase demonstration fits that instructional structure: showing how an interface works is not, by itself, evidence that its advertised returns will materialize or that the creator controls them.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening cites a real buying walkthrough, but it omits the surrounding explanation of node costs, reward choices and the project's own documentation. Even the introductory invitation is conditional: the speaker says viewers may proceed if they decide to take the risk. That framing supports reading the walkthrough as an operational demonstration, though it does not validate the project's claims.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Using a PDF as teaching material does not make the video neutral. The speaker calls the project sustainable and trustworthy, explains that buying tokens unlocks daily rewards, and then demonstrates how to purchase and create a node. The instructional format is part of how viewers are moved toward the paid-node offer.

opening.argument: Judge, the observable transaction is an explained token-and-node purchase, not evidence that this creator collects viewers' deposits or credentials. He describes using a wallet and approving a contract, while plainly stating that the token cost is not recoverable and that maintenance fees continue. His separate mentorship offer is identified as his own service, and the description discloses that some links may pay him a commission. None of that proves the external node service is safe, but the cited record does not establish a hidden payment route or a guaranteed return from the creator.

His mentorship invitation is a separate offer. The recurring rewards are described as a feature of the node, while the record also states the upfront tokens are gone and maintenance fees apply.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern does not depend on proving that the creator personally receives node payments or requests credentials. He promotes a mechanism in which viewers buy tokens to create a node that purportedly pays daily rewards, then gives the steps to do it. The unrecoverable token cost and continuing fees heighten the stakes of that promotion; an affiliate disclosure does not change what is being offered.
